correctness.rationale: For every odd-order finite abelian group, Fourier inversion is an isomorphism. The exact cycle polynomial z^(2^ell)=z counts all complex idempotents. Character inversion gives necessary and sufficient realness; its action on each self-dual nontrivial cycle is the half-turn, leaving 2^(ell/2)+1 nonzero compatible roots. Multiplication by an idempotent on a Fourier orbit is zero or a weighted cycle whose weights multiply to one, proving characteristic polynomial t^ell or t^ell−1. All quantifiers, boundary groups and prime-order formula follow, with numerical full finite-instance corroboration in verify.py.

originality.rationale: The independently assessed extension is the exact real idempotent and Peirce-characteristic-polynomial distribution for every finite medial commutative midpoint quandle. Zhang already supplies the Fourier idempotent equation, so its immediate complex cardinality corollary is explicitly excluded as a standalone novelty claim. Additional arguments classify self-dual and paired character cycles under complex conjugation and determine right-multiplication monomial blocks; the resulting multivariate spectral enumerators and contrasting order-nine real counts are not covered in the inspected primary material.
residual_risks: The published Fourier equation is a strong premise; only the additional real-arithmetic and Peirce-distribution results are asserted as original.
Other nonassociative-algebra or permutation/Fourier literature may contain an equivalent orbit census under different terminology.
The public three-element comparison was summary-level only; it is not taken as evidence about any larger family.
Independent literature review and external mathematical validation remain outstanding.

value.rationale: Real idempotent counts and the full Peirce polynomial/rank distribution are intrinsic invariants of finite medial commutative quandle algebras, naturally motivated by existing knot-theoretic idempotent constructions and Peirce-spectrum questions. The exact formulas extend across every finite odd-order abelian group. Real counts 80 and 512 separate the two nine-element midpoint quandles although complex totals coincide, showing genuinely arithmetic information not supplied by the prior integral theory. The result does not rely on a broad unproved application claim.
